plays.overview: Turn red, blue and purple teaming from periodic assessments into a continuous loop, built foundations first, humans in command.
plays.humancommand: AI amplifies human judgment rather than replacing it: people own strategy, policy and the big decisions, and agents earn autonomy.
plays.foundations: AI multiplies whatever it lands on, so build the five SOC fundamentals first, with AI helping to lay them, before scaling autonomy.
plays.red: Agents emulate adversaries continuously, chain ATT&CK and ATLAS techniques, and test your own AI and MCP attack surface.
plays.blue: Triage agents turn raw alerts into pre-analyzed cases, freeing analysts for judgment while hunting and detection scale up.
plays.purple: The heart of the strategy: red executes, blue detects, both close the gap, and agents run the loop with autonomy as a dial.
plays.maturity: A four-level ladder from AI-assisted work to autonomous SecOps, so you can place your SOC and see what the next level asks.
plays.roadmap: A phased path from assessment and baseline to scaling toward autonomy, each phase with key moves and an exit criterion to meet first.
plays.program: The management view: the first 90 days, who owns what, build versus buy, and a workforce plan for the analysts.
plays.metrics: Speed, quality, coverage and cost measures that show whether the program works, with every speed metric paired to a quality metric.
plays.actionplan: Every recommended action in the playbook in one sequenced list, Now, Next and Later, each linked back to the play it comes from.
plays.architecture: A seven-layer reference architecture, read as defensive design and as the attacker's view, with six principles applied at every layer.
plays.infra: The engineering factors behind deploying agents: token economics, compute, hosting, storage and scaling, as factors to baseline.
plays.netsec: Firewalls and AI gateways, egress filtering, segmentation, monitoring and identity controls that bound an agentic deployment.
plays.otics: In OT, safety and availability come first, so the bar for agent autonomy rises sharply and the IT/OT boundary is the hard line.
plays.governance: Governance as the control plane: every agent action authorized, scoped, logged and reviewable, and mapped to a framework.
plays.compliance: The EU AI Act, NIS2, DORA, ISO 42001 and the US picture: the dated obligations your controls and audit trail must satisfy.
plays.federal: How agentic AI fits federal authorization: FISMA, FedRAMP, DoD impact levels, continuous ATO, CUI and classified networks.
plays.vendor: Vet the models, vendors and components you adopt: keep an AI bill of materials, check provenance, and plan for continuity.
plays.threatmodel: Work out how an AI system can be attacked before it ships, pairing STRIDE, MAESTRO and NIST with a use-case-first method.
plays.threats: The AI-specific threat taxonomy, real incidents and the feeds tracking them, to steer red TTPs and blue detection coverage.
plays.cti: Intelligence drives operations: CTI tells red agents what to emulate, blue agents what to hunt, and leaders where to invest.
plays.insiders: Treat each agent as a privileged non-human insider, with Zero Trust verification, monitoring and a full identity lifecycle.
plays.containment: Model defenses are never 100%, so sandboxes, egress controls and circuit breakers cap an agent's blast radius first.
plays.agentir: When the agent itself is the incident: detect, investigate, contain, preserve, recover and learn, with a runbook for your own agents.
plays.cscrm: C-SCRM through a counterintelligence lens: how an adversary would weaponize your AI supply chain, and how to disrupt it.
plays.frontier: The frontier lab and government programs at the leading edge of AI security, and why public-private partnership matters.
plays.frameworks: The authoritative references for an AI security program, from the NIST AI RMF and OWASP to MAESTRO, and what each anchors.
plays.academic: Independent university research and key arXiv papers that ground the playbook's claims, a counterweight to vendor sources.
plays.cases: Documented cases from 2025 to 2026, in offense and defense, each told as what happened and what it proves.
plays.risks: The critical risks of agentic SecOps, from the lethal trifecta to blast radius and trusted-user abuse, with guardrails for each.
plays.tools: The frameworks, platforms and products that make agentic SecOps real today, from orchestration to red team automation.
plays.fluency: A working glossary of the terms that recur across the plays: agentic foundations, attacks, defense, CTI, and federal and DoW.
plays.learningpath: A three-to-four-week self-study path from what an AI agent is to running red, blue and purple exercises, with labs and courses.
plays.resources: All 243 key sources behind the playbook, grouped by theme, from frameworks and federal standards to threat intelligence.
